USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Two platelet pathways

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

After PCI for acute coronary syndrome, a patient without excessive bleeding risk is prescribed aspirin and a P2Y12 inhibitor. He asks why two antiplatelet drugs are used. Which explanation best describes this treatment strategy?

  1. They inhibit complementary platelet activation pathways
  2. Both drugs are interchangeable anticoagulants acting on thrombin
  3. One drug activates platelets while the other inhibits them
  4. Both directly remove cholesterol from an existing plaque
  5. The second drug is used only to treat aspirin-induced fever
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

They inhibit complementary platelet activation pathways

Dual antiplatelet therapy combines aspirin-mediated thromboxane inhibition with P2Y12 receptor blockade.

Understanding the options

They inhibit complementary platelet activation pathways
Dual antiplatelet therapy combines aspirin-mediated thromboxane inhibition with P2Y12 receptor blockade.
Both drugs are interchangeable anticoagulants acting on thrombin
They are antiplatelet agents with distinct targets.
One drug activates platelets while the other inhibits them
Both inhibit platelet activation.
Both directly remove cholesterol from an existing plaque
They do not work by physically removing plaque cholesterol.
The second drug is used only to treat aspirin-induced fever
The P2Y12 inhibitor provides antiplatelet activity.
